response: PORTRAIT: 7 controls - SPY | 1D | draw | broker | ••• | undo | redo(clipped). LANDSCAPE: 14 controls - SPY | 1D | draw | INDICATORS | LAYOUTS | broker | ADD | ALERTS | (settings) | BAR REPLAY | OBJECT TREE/layers | ••• | undo | redo(still clipped)
result: SIX+ TOOLS ARE PROMOTED FROM THE ANALYSIS HUB TO THE PERSISTENT TOOLBAR IN LANDSCAPE
notes: ⭐⭐ HEADLINE ARCHITECTURAL FINDING. Interaction depth for indicators, alerts, bar replay, layouts and object tree HALVES on rotation: 2 taps (••• then tool) in portrait becomes 1 tap in landscape. TradingView does not hide controls in landscape - it PROMOTES them, using the extra horizontal budget to flatten navigation depth. This is a deliberate depth-vs-width trade, and it is the correct mental model for anyone designing a phone chart: the hub exists because portrait lacks width, not because the tools are secondary.

The implication for UCT is that a landscape mode should probably also change PANE POLICY, not just width.

notes: NEW ROW. TradingView does NOT treat landscape as an immersive full-screen chart mode by default - global navigation is retained, costing vertical space in the orientation where vertical space is scarcest. A separate full-screen control exists (see the drawing-mode toolbar's fullscreen icon), suggesting immersion is opt-in rather than implied by rotation.

action: Inspect the right end of the landscape toolbar
response: Redo remains horizontally CLIPPED by the screen edge even with 14 controls and full landscape width
result: THE TOOLBAR OVERFLOWS IN BOTH ORIENTATIONS
notes: CORROBORATES UNDO-0012 and strengthens it: this is not a portrait-width accident. TradingView adds MORE controls in landscape rather than fixing the clip, so redo is the least-reachable control in both orientations. For a touch surface where accidental gestures are the dominant error mode, having the recovery control permanently half-off-screen is a real error-tolerance defect - and one UCT should not replicate.
